title: Priority Tapestry: Interlock Patterns & Initiative Handoff Playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Purpose: Create a concise, repeatable playbook that operationalizes company-level OKRs into cross-functional initiatives with clear interlock patterns, handoff primitives, and escalation paths. Scope: company-level OKRs and the set of initiatives that span Eng, Product, Design, Research, and GTM teams. Excludes team-level backlog planning templates. Goals: 1) Reduce cross-team misalignment during quarter handoffs by 50% (measured by number of blocked handoffs and missed milestones). 2) Standardize three interlock patterns (Serial, Parallel with Sync Points, Hub-and-Spoke) and associated artifact checklist. 3) Provide a low-friction handoff process for initiative ownership, dependencies, and roll-forward decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page playbook document in Confluence with step-by-step handoff flow
Three canonical interlock pattern templates with example responsibilities mapped to RACI
A lightweight handoff checklist (Google Sheet + template) used by two pilot initiatives
A retrospective template and dashboard query showing pre/post handoff metrics for pilot initiatives
approach_summary: Run two parallel pilots (one infra-heavy, one product-experience initiative) over a single cycle. Draft playbook, collect feedback from PM/Eng/Design leads, iterate and publish as 'Company Playbook v0.1'. Integrate handoff checklist with Console rollout gating in a follow-up piece of work.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Keep playbook lightweight vs. making it comprehensive — risk of low adoption if too heavy
Pilot only two initiatives (fast feedback) vs. larger cohort (broader signals). We choose fast feedback first
Dependencies on ENG and Console teams for rollout gating integration may delay release
success_metrics: Adoption: >= 70% of cross-functional initiatives in Q4 use the checklist
Alignment: 50% reduction in blocked handoffs for pilot initiatives vs previous quarter
Quality: At least 3 actionable improvements captured from pilot retrospectives
